paper.title: More Adaptive Algorithms for Adversarial Bandits

unmapped: action set X is an arbitrary subset of {0,1}^K; K_0 = max ||b||_0
settings.definition_quote: In each round, the learner selects a subset of arms, denoted by a binary vector $b_t$ from a predefined action set $\mathcal{X}\subseteq \{0,1\}^K$, and suffers loss $b_t^\top \ell_t$, where $\ell_t \in [-1,1]^K$ is a loss vector decided by an adversary. ... we assume that the adversary is oblivious
In the special case of multi-armed bandit, the action set $\mathcal{X}$ is $\{\mathbf{e}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{e}_K\}$ ... receives the loss $\ell_{t,i_t}$.
in the adversarial setting, we have $\mathbb{E}[\reg_T] = \mathcal{O}(\sqrt{KL_{T,i^*}\ln T}+K\ln T)$ assuming non-negative losses.

settings.name_in_paper: stochastic setting with fixed conditional gap
unmapped: E[l_{t,i} - l_{t,a*} | l_1..l_{t-1}] >= Delta for all i != a*, t; neither independence nor identical distribution required (no corruption term)
regret measured against the empirically best arm i*, expectation also over losses
settings.definition_quote: there exists an arm $a^*$ and some fixed gap $\Delta > 0$ such that $\mathbb{E}_{\ell_t}\left[\ell_{t,i}-\ell_{t,a^*} | \ell_1, \ldots, \ell_{t-1}\right]\geq \Delta$ for all $i \neq a^*$ and $t\in[T]$.

settings.name_in_paper: two-player zero-sum game with bandit feedback
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Game-theoretic convergence to Nash equilibrium in repeated zero-sum games, not a regret guarantee for a bandit problem
unmapped: players observe e_{i_t}^T G y_t (expected loss of own realized action)
objective is convergence of average strategies to Nash equilibrium value; players are competitive, not cooperative
settings.definition_quote: The game is defined by an unknown matrix $G\in[-1,1]^{M\times N}$ ... we consider a setting where the feedbacks are the scalar values $\mathbf{e}_{i_t}^\top Gy_t$ and $x_t^\top G\mathbf{e}_{j_t}$ respectively

symbols.K_0: max number of arms an action can pick, max_b ||b||_0
symbols.E_err: E[sum_t sum_{i in b*} (l_{t,i} - m_{t,i})^2], squared prediction error on the best action's arms

source.label: cor:clear_corollary
source.quote: Broad-OMD with $a_{t,i}=6\eta_{t,i}w_{t,i}(\hat{\ell}_{t,i}-m_{t,i})^2$, any $m_{t,i} \in [-1, 1]$, $\hat{\ell}_{t,i}=\frac{(\ell_{t,i}-m_{t,i})\mathbbm{1}\{i\in b_t\}}{w_{t,i}}+m_{t,i}$, and $\eta_{t,i}=\eta \leq \frac{1}{162K_0}$ enjoys ... \leq \frac{K\ln T}{\eta} + 6\eta\mathbb{E}[...] +\mathcal{O}(K_0).

results.notes: Only the additive K_0 term is in O(); first two terms have explicit constants. Recorded with notation O.

symbols.Q_star: unnormalized variance of the best arm's losses, sum_t (l_{t,i*} - mu_{T,i*})^2

tuning: reservoir sampling with M = Theta(ln T)

source.label: cor:variance_bound
source.quote: Broad-OMD with reservoir sampling~\citep{hazan2011better}, ..., $m_{t,i}=\tilde{\mu}_{t-1,i}$, ... and $\eta_{t,i}=\eta\leq \frac{1}{162}$ guarantees $\mathbb{E}[\reg_T]= \mathcal{O}(\frac{K\ln T}{\eta}+\eta Q_{T,i^*} + K(\ln T)^2)$. With the optimal tuning of $\eta$, the regret is thus of order $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{KQ_{T,i^*}}+K)$.

results.notes: Q_star is the best arm's variance, not the canonical quadratic variation Q_T.

symbols.Q_star: unnormalized variance of the best arm's losses

tuning: eta optimally tuned using Q_{T,i*} (unknown quantity)
reservoir sampling with M = Theta(ln T)

source.label: cor:variance_bound
source.quote: With the optimal tuning of $\eta$, the regret is thus of order $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sqrt{KQ_{T,i^*}}+K\right)$.

results.notes: Requires tuning eta with knowledge of Q_{T,i*}, not in vocabulary.

symbols.V_star: first-order path length of the best arm, sum_t |l_{t,i*} - l_{t-1,i*}|

tuning: m_{t,i} = most recently observed loss of arm i

source.label: thm:path_length
source.quote: Broad-OMD+ with $m_{t,i}=\ell_{\alpha_i(t), i}$ and $\eta_{1,i}=\eta\leq \frac{1}{810}$ guarantees $\mathbb{E}[\reg_T ] \leq \frac{2K\ln T}{\eta} + \mathbb{E}[\rho_{T+1,i^*}]( \frac{-1}{40\eta\ln T} + 90\eta V_{T,i^*} ) + \mathcal{O}( 1 )$ when $T\geq 3$. Picking $\eta = \min\{\frac{1}{810}, \frac{1}{60\sqrt{V_{T,i^*} \ln T}}\}$ ... leads to $\mathbb{E}[\reg_T ] = \tilde{\mathcal{O}}( K\sqrt{V_{T,i^*}}+K )$.

results.notes: The intermediate bound involving E[rho_{T+1,i*}] is not recorded separately; tuning requires knowledge of V_{T,i*}.

symbols.K_0: max number of arms an action can pick

conditions: w_{t,i}|hat l_{t,i} - m_{t,i}| <= 3 and eta sum_i w_{t,i}^2 (hat l_{t,i}-m_{t,i})^2 <= 1/18 (conditions (ii),(iii) of Theorem 7)
tuning: initial eta = 1/(162 K_0), halved at each restart

source.label: thm:doubling_trick_theorem
source.quote: If conditions (ii) and (iii) in Theorem~\ref{lemma:second_order_regret_bound} hold, then Algorithm \ref{alg:doubling} guarantees $\mathbb{E}[\reg_T]=\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{(K\ln T)\mathbb{E}[\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^Kw_{t,i}^2(\hat{\ell}_{t,i}-m_{t,i})^2]}+K_0K\ln T)$.

results.notes: Bound in terms of an algorithm-dependent quantity; conditions (ii),(iii) are on estimator/prediction choices.

symbols.V_sum: sum over all arms of first-order path lengths, sum_i sum_t |l_{t,i} - l_{t-1,i}|

tuning: m_{t,i} = most recently observed loss of arm i

source.label: cor:path_length_bound_1
source.quote: Broad-OMD with $a_{t,i}=0$, $m_{t,i}=\ell_{\alpha_i(t),i}$, ..., and $\eta_{t,i}=\eta\leq \frac{1}{162}$ guarantees $\mathbb{E}[\reg_T]\leq\mathcal{O}(\frac{K\ln T}{\eta}) + 6\eta\sum_{i=1}^K V_{T,i} -\mathbb{E}[\sum_{t=2}^{T} \sum_{i=1}^K\frac{(w_{t,i}-w_{t-1,i})^2}{48\eta w_{t-1,i}^2} ]\leq \mathcal{O}( \frac{K\ln T}{\eta} + \eta\sum_{i=1}^K V_{T,i} ).

results.notes: Finer bound includes negative stability term; recorded the simplified O bound.

symbols.V_sum: sum over all arms of first-order path lengths

tuning: m_{t,i} = most recently observed loss of arm i

source.label: cor:path_length_bound_1
source.quote: Using the doubling trick (Algorithm~\ref{alg:doubling}), we achieve expected regret $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left(\sqrt{K\sum_{i=1}^K V_{T,i}} + K\right)$.

symbols.X_exc: E[sum_t sum_i (l_{t,i} 1{i_t=i} - w_{t,i} l_{t,i_t})^2], second-order excess loss quantity

source.label: thm:best of both
source.quote: Broad-OMD with $a_t = 0$, $m_{t,i}=\ell_{t,i_t}$, $\hat{\ell}_{t,i}=\frac{\ell_{t,i}\mathbbm{1}\{i_t=i\}}{w_{t,i}}$, and the doubling trick (Algorithm~\ref{alg:doubling}), guarantees $\mathbb{E}[\reg_T]=\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{(K\ln T)\mathbb{E}[ \sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{i=1}^K (\ell_{t,i}\mathbbm{1}\{i_t=i\}-w_{t,i}\ell_{t,i_t})^2 ]} + K\ln T )$.

conditions: exists arm a* with E[l_{t,i} - l_{t,a*} | l_1..l_{t-1}] >= Delta for all i != a*

source.label: thm:best of both
source.quote: This bound implies that in the stochastic setting, we have $\mathbb{E}\left[\reg_T\right] = \mathcal{O}\left(\frac{K\ln T}{\Delta}\right)$

results.notes: Delta is the uniform gap shared by all suboptimal arms; regret vs empirical best arm i*, expectation over losses and learner. Same algorithm also gives r10 (best of both worlds); learner does not know Delta.

source.label: thm:best of both
source.quote: while in the adversarial setting, we have $\mathbb{E}\left[\reg_T\right] = \mathcal{O}\left(\sqrt{KL_{T,i^*}\ln T}+K\ln T\right)$ assuming non-negative losses.

results.notes: Small-loss bound; L_{T,i*} is cumulative loss of best arm.

conditions: both players run Broad-OMD as in Corollary 9

source.label: thm:fast_convergence_theorem
source.quote: if both players run Broad-OMD configured as in Corollary~\ref{cor:path_length_bound_1} except that $\eta_{t,i}=\eta= (M+N)^{-\frac{1}{4}}T^{-\frac{1}{4}}$, then their expected average strategies converge to Nash equilibriums at the rate of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left((M+N)^{\frac{5}{4}}/T^{\frac{3}{4}}\right)$

results.notes: Convergence rate of expected average strategies' duality gap to the game value; out of scope.

cited_results.setting_description: adversarial multi-armed bandit, K arms, T rounds

applied.reason: The two players of a zero-sum game are competitive, not cooperative; the vocabulary term should not be stretched.
applied.evidence: entry $G(i,j)$ specifies the loss (or reward) for Player 1 (or Player 2)

_verify.summary: The extraction is accurate. The expressions, constants, settings and provenance match the paper for all main results (Corollary 3, Theorems 4, 5, 8, 10, Corollary 9 and Theorem 20). The only issue is that the zero-sum game setting is tagged as cooperative multi-agent, although the two players compete.
